source.title: Complexity Scaling for Speech Denoising
source.authors: Hangting Chen; Jianwei Yu; Chao Weng

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests performance scaling in a new setting, speech denoising, using objective denoising metrics versus computational cost rather than language-model held-out loss versus parameters, tokens, or training compute.
record.gate_note: The study reports a fitted scaling relationship for PESQ-WB and SI-SNR across MPT computational costs, plus individual DNS test results and architecture ablations. It does not test language-model loss scaling, small-run extrapolation, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, or downstream language-task predictability. The ablations are included as results about architecture and matched-complexity denoising performance, not as direct tests of V4.
record.test_reason: It fits how speech-denoising quality (PESQ-WB, SI-SNR) scales with compute across causal MPT models from 50M to 15G MACs/s, about 2.5 orders of magnitude. That is a scaling-form result in a non-text modality, which bears on V5. It does not measure loss, training compute, parameters or tokens.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also call the relation a power law and state it for causal models below 15G MACs/s: about +0.09 PESQ and +0.36 dB SI-SNR per doubling of compute. They describe it as the first scaling law for speech denoising.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a fixed denoising dataset and varies MPT computational complexity; measures PESQ-WB and SI-SNR rather than language-model held-out loss against parameter, token, and training-compute scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Model configuration changes with computational cost, including MPT block count and expansion settings; the paper also reports that transformer selection, mask type, and use of deep filtering affect denoising metrics in ablations.

fits_no_version.finding: At roughly matched MACs, denoising metrics vary with the transformer subset used, the mask type and deep filtering. Example: PESQ ranges 2.02–2.21 at about 100M/s.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Speech-denoising performance at similar computational cost depends on architectural component choices.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper provides a demo and detailed-results URL: https://hangtingchen.github.io/Complexity-Scaling-for-Speech-Denoising.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: The reported scaling fit uses objective denoising metrics rather than loss. The text gives no uncertainty estimates for the fitted formulas or table values. The dataset is fixed, and the text says only PESQ-WB and SI-SNR are listed in the paper.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separately reported MPT metric or ablation results in Tables 2–3 were omitted.

untested.parts: Loss-based scaling; scaling in training compute, parameters or dataset size (the dataset is fixed and compute is inference MACs/s); extrapolation beyond the fitted range; other modalities and regimes.
Not tested: no prediction of larger runs from small fits.
Not tested: the ablations swap components (transformer subsets, mask type, deep filtering), not depth or width at fixed parameters.
Not tested: there is a single fit with no comparison of fitting choices.

missing.what: MPT points at 50M, 195M, 502M and 4.1G MACs/s that enter the Fig. 1 fit. Their values are not in the text, so they need reading from the figure or the demo page.
Goodness of fit and uncertainty for the log-linear fit; none are reported.

record.verdict_notes: The fit formula only reproduces Table 2 when MACs/s is expressed in millions. Seven Table 2 rows (R04, R09, R10, R13, R14, R17, R18) carry values shifted from neighbouring models, apparently from table misparsing. The 'power law' reading for SI-SNR is my inference from dB being a log ratio; the paper does not derive it.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits to small runs.
Compute-optimal allocation between language-model parameters and training tokens.
Loss at fixed parameter count across depth, width, and other language-model architecture choices; the paper's ablations use denoising metrics and approximately matched MACs instead.
Other non-text modalities and regimes beyond speech denoising; loss-based scaling; the study uses objective denoising metrics and a fixed dataset.
Downstream language-task performance and its predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
Whether fitted language-model exponents or compute-optimal splits vary with parameter counting, schedules, data, or fitting choices; whether such curves bend away from a single power law.

conditions.value: DNS-2020 no reverb / with reverb; PESQ reported as averaged score

rows.note: The paper describes the relationship as linear in log2 MACs/s and gives this fitted formula.
rows.check: The fit is log-linear in a bounded perceptual score against inference MACs/s, not a power law in loss. The intercept only matches Table 2 if MACs/s is in millions, e.g. 102M gives a predicted 2.69 vs an actual mean of 2.665.

rows.check: Units are millions of MACs/s. SI-SNR is in dB, so +0.36 dB per doubling means the residual error-to-signal ratio falls about as compute^-0.12, which is a power law. The fit matches Table 2 MPT means within about 0.07 dB.

relationships.condition: Causal MPT speech-denoising models, 50M–15G MACs/s, DNS-2020 averaged test sets, SI-SNR
relationships.reason: SI-SNR rises 0.36 dB per compute doubling and fits Table 2 points closely (R02). This implies residual error ratio falls as a power law of compute, roughly C^-0.12.
relationships.display_finding: SI-SNR improved by 0.36 dB per compute doubling, implying a residual-error ratio scaling approximately as C^−0.12.

relationships.condition: Same sweep, PESQ-WB; compute counted as inference MACs/s with architecture changing across sizes
relationships.reason: PESQ is log-linear in compute for a bounded score capped near 4.5, not a power law (R01). The sweep also switches GRU to LSTM above 1G and varies block count, so the form is tied to a changing architecture.
relationships.display_finding: PESQ followed a log-linear compute trend toward a ceiling near 4.5, while architectures switched from GRU to LSTM above 1G MACs/s and varied in block number.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: MPT speech-denoising models on the DNS-2020 test sets, across the reported 50M/s–15G/s computational-cost sweep
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports increasing objective metrics with log2 computational cost and gives fitted formulas for PESQ-WB and SI-SNR (R01–R02). This supports the power-law-like form for these metrics in this tested audio setting, not for loss.
